public_evidence.observation: Calle Luchetti is manifested as a Villalba address/toponym.
Antonio Luchetti Street appears as a historical Villalba street-name manifestation.
DTOP's 2023 HPMS log uses CALLE LUCHETTI as a Villalba roadway reference at PR-5149, independently confirming the Luchetti spelling in the state road inventory context.

Villalba's approved hazard mitigation plan lists the AEE hydroelectric plant at Calle Lucchetti, Bda. Cooperativa, preserving the double-c spelling as an official planning manifestation and independently tying the street to hydroelectric context.
PREPA/PREB material places Toro Negro I hydroelectric infrastructure on Calle Luchetti and separately manifests the street as Calle Antonio Lucchetti.
Puerto Rico planning material states that the Antonio Lucchetti dam/lake name honors engineer Antonio Lucchetti; the source family contains Lucchetti/Luchetti spelling variation.

A contemporary Puerto Rico public-works journal identifies Antonio Luchetti as chief engineer of the South Coast Irrigation Service in reporting on irrigation and Fuentes Fluviales, strengthening the historical infrastructure-eponym context without directly naming the Villalba street.

contradictions_and_variants.disposition: PRESERVE_BOTH; both forms occur in authoritative/public-source manifestations; spelling variation cannot establish identity, naming origin, or error direction by itself

public_search_residue: Villalba municipal ordinance or dedication record explicitly naming the street for Antonio Lucchetti
contemporaneous street-register entry with naming authority and effective date
equivalent authoritative documentary binding between the street and engineer Antonio Lucchetti

search_disposition.result: Additional authoritative street and hydro-context manifestations were recovered, but no direct street-naming instrument was located. The direct eponym proposition therefore remains provisional rather than promoted.

certification.bounded_claim: Publicly located evidence supports a real Villalba Calle/Antonio Luchetti-Lucchetti street manifestation by at least 1965, multiple modern authoritative spelling manifestations, and independent hydroelectric context, but does not directly bind the street's naming origin to Antonio Lucchetti.
